name: Acme Robotics
engineeringPractices: Trunk-based development, roughly 20 deploys a day
One-week on-call rotation, engineers own their services in production
Design docs circulate for 48h before any cross-team change
culture: Written-first — proposals go out as documents before meetings happen
Hardware release cycles create genuine crunch in the weeks before customer pilots
Strong internal mobility; several ML engineers started on the backend team

negative: compensation lags the London market by 10-15%
pre-launch crunch is real and recurring

name: Northwind Health
engineeringPractices: Two-week sprints with a formal release train
Every change touching patient data needs a second reviewer and an audit entry
Heavy automated compliance testing; CI runs about 40 minutes
culture: Process-heavy by necessity — regulated environment, and it shows in the pace
Excellent work-life balance; on-call is rare and genuinely compensated
Slower to adopt new technology than most engineers coming from startups expect

negative: legacy Java services nobody wants to own

name: Lumen Fintech
engineeringPractices: Small autonomous squads, each owning a payment rail end to end
No dedicated QA — engineers write and own their tests
Incident reviews are blameless and published company-wide
culture: High autonomy, high expectation — very little direction is given, which suits some people and not others
Growing fast enough that roles change under you every few months

negative: onboarding is thin, expect to self-serve

name: Tessellate AI
engineeringPractices: Ship-to-main daily; feature flags over long-lived branches
Research and product engineers sit in the same team, no handoff
culture: Intense pace — the company is explicit that this is not a balanced-hours environment
Flat structure, founders still review code
In-office four days a week in SF, no remote option for engineers

negative: burnout is common and openly acknowledged

name: Harbour Logistics
engineeringPractices: Profitable and unhurried — quarterly planning, no crunch culture
Strong internal platform team; product engineers rarely touch infrastructure
Pairing is the default for anything non-trivial
culture: Genuinely 40-hour weeks, and management enforces it
Long tenure — the median engineer has been there over five years
Conservative technology choices; expect to work on systems, not greenfield

positive: best work-life balance in the industry
negative: compensation below market for senior levels

name: Vertex Media
engineeringPractices: Service-per-team ownership with a strong SRE function
Rigorous A/B testing culture — most features ship behind an experiment
Quarterly architecture review board for cross-cutting changes
culture: Scale problems are real and interesting; organisational politics are also real
Very strong for frontend and streaming-infrastructure careers specifically
Team quality varies widely — the interview is as much you assessing them

negative: promotion depends heavily on your manager
